correctness.rationale: Hermitian invariant spectators give orthogonal Gaussian columns, hence the random determinant factors and the non-spectator root has the exact shifted-scaled ratio law for independent standard circular complex normals. The complex-Cauchy law has infinite second moment, whereas the real median-of-three density integrates to variance one-half per coordinate, yielding exactly the squared eigen-residual as the repaired mean-square error. Binomial sample-median tails establish the if-and-only-if sharp odd-sample moment classification. All dimension, normalization, and nonzero-residual boundary hypotheses were checked analytically; the 585 finite numerical pencil tests corroborate but do not prove the result.

originality.rationale: The novel claim is a spectral-pencil-specific law plus a sharp three-independent-sketch residual-MSE identity and odd-replication moment cutoff. The quotient distribution and sample-median calculus are established probabilistic tools and not claimed independently new. The closest 2026 randomized Ritz paper gives high-probability bounds/refined outputs, whereas a prior sketched Ritz method uses a rectangular pseudoinverse. The checked primary results do not imply the exact unrefined spectral risk and median identity. Full equivalence risk remains for unindexed studies.

The exact result does not cover arbitrary Ritz-root selection or nonlinear/non-Hermitian pencils.

value.rationale: Unconditional mean-square accuracy is a natural complement to the new high-probability convergence theory for unrefined randomized Ritz values. The exact invariant-spectator model shows infinite raw MSE for arbitrarily small residual, gives an exact constructive repair with only three independent original square sketches, and determines an iff moment budget for every odd replication count. The MSE equals the meaningful deterministic eigen-residual squared, dimension-free, for arbitrary Hermitian matrices under a natural deflation structure. This does not purport to outperform deterministic Hermitian Rayleigh-quotient refinement.
